Discrete Symmetries

Source: R/symmetryDetection.R
discreteSymmetries.Rd

Searches the discrete symmetries of a symmetryDetection() result: other points of the domain with the output of a given one. The Taylor coefficients of the observables up to order are equated with their values at a point; msolve counts the solutions over the algebraic closure modulo a prime, and over the reals and in the declared domain at points random rational points, where the number in the domain may differ between regions. Where the other points are rational functions \(\sigma\) of the coordinates, \(\sigma\) is reconstructed, checked on the output at random points ("checked") and, where every state has a free initial value, proven by a map of the states ("exact"). A model with directions is reduced by symmetryReduction() first and the reduced model is analyzed. The search stops on work limits, never on a clock, so the result is the same on every machine; a count or proof that reaches a limit ends without a result and names the limit in limits or in the certificate.

Usage

discreteSymmetries(
  object,
  order = NULL,
  points = 5L,
  cores = 1,
  memory = NULL,
  experiments = NULL,
  msolveEntries = NULL,
  msolveTerms = NULL,
  searchEntries = NULL,
  eliminationTerms = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A symmetrydetection result from symmetryDetection().

order

Highest Taylor coefficient; NULL (default) twice the number of coordinates.

points

Number of random points of the count in the domain, or a list of points, each a named list of the coordinates. Defaults to 5.

cores

Threads of msolve. Defaults to 1.

memory

GiB of address space one call of msolve may take; past it the call fails. NULL (default) keeps the value of symident (8).

experiments

Count on several experiments with shared parameters and free starts, which bounds the fiber of a model with free starts and no rational first integral: NULL (default) where a short count of one experiment finds none, TRUE first with the number of experiments from the rank criterion, a number K with K experiments, FALSE never.

msolveEntries

Nonzero entries of the F4 matrices one call of msolve may reduce.

msolveTerms

Terms of the largest system given to msolve.

searchEntries

Entries of the matrices over finite fields the exact count may reduce.

eliminationTerms

Terms of the largest polynomial of the elimination of the states in the exact count.

Value

object with discreteSymmetries, per \(\sigma\) the map of the coordinates it changes (an eqnvec), changes, level, preservesDomain (TRUE, FALSE, or NULL with the domainConditions under which \(\sigma(\theta)\) lies in the domain) and fixedSet, the factors on which \(\sigma\) fixes \(\theta\); and info$discrete with order, count (the solutions over the algebraic closure at a random point modulo a prime), countBound (the probability that a generic point has more, NULL where the count is exact or has no bound), countDomain (the points of the fiber of a generic point inside the domain, where that number is final), counts per point (complex, real, inDomain, undecided), closedForms, countFinal (every solution is the image of a proven \(\sigma\)), fundamentalDomain (inequalities that keep one point of each orbit), certificate (what the result rests on, with complete: "exact", "verified", "axiom", "no" or "open"), experiments (the count on several experiments, or why it does not apply), limits and, where they apply, reduced (for a model with directions), eliminated (under reduceCQ, the species solved through the totals), relaxed (the model with non-rational terms of the states as new states) and unsupported.

Details

The search needs msolve; symmetryDetection() says where it is searched. The defaults of msolveEntries, msolveTerms, searchEntries and eliminationTerms (NULL) keep the values of symident.

References

Godfrey, K. (1983). Compartmental Models and Their Application. Academic Press, London.

See also

symmetryDetection(), symmetryReduction()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) && reticulate::py_module_available("symident.install") && !is.null(tryCatch(reticulate::import("symident.install")$find_msolve()[[1]], error = function(e) NULL))
# two compartments, an input u into the first, the second observed
f <- eqnvec(x1 = "-(k21 + k01)*x1 + k12*x2 + u", x2 = "k21*x1 - k12*x2")
res <- symmetryDetection(f, eqnvec(y = "x2"), knownInputs = "u", mode = "global")
res
res$discreteSymmetries[[1]]$map
res$info$discrete$fundamentalDomain
}
